parsed.explanation: This state/province layer is comparatively protective—public-accommodations and health-care anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence repeal, and a 2026 civil-rights judgment—but the national layer governs border screening, immigration custody, national facilities, and much care policy. A trans visitor with a document/presentation mismatch can be refused entry or tagged for possible lifetime fraud inadmissibility; national custody carries documented abuse; national facility rules restrict sex-segregated access in government-funded settings; national threat-framing and minor-care bans add chilling effect. Local protections do not reach these national encounters, though they lower everyday street/service risk. The combined regime is therefore Elevated Risk, not Reduced Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy processes only M/F markers, has stopped X-marker processing, and border cable directs refusal/additional evidence where sex is doubted; suspected wilful misrepresentation can support permanent fraud inadmissibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation and legal-aid guidance are pending, but local anti-discrimination law does not control national border screening.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport with X or a marker/presentation mismatch can move from secondary inspection to refusal, stranding, or a lifetime ineligibility finding under national immigration rules.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody has documented forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of transgender detainees; national corrections policies impose conversion-style practices on trans inmates.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law and court injunctions against some executive orders exist, and local civil-rights law is enforceable, but neither is documented as reaching national immigration custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border fraud inquiry or immigration hold places the visitor in national custody, where local protections and local courts do not govern placement or treatment.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A national executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; some state/provinces criminalise bathroom use, though this state/province is not documented as one.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has public-accommodations anti-discrimination covering gender identity since 2018 and no documented local bathroom ban; enforcement in local venues is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National buildings and federally funded facilities follow the national restriction, while local protections may cover private and state-covered venues; the harshest operative rule governs the outed traveller's encounter.

care_services.exposure: State/province law bans gender-affirming medicine and surgery for minors, with provider discipline and a right to sue; national policy pressures minor care and public insurance.
care_services.protection: State/province anti-discrimination covers health care, conversion therapy on minors is banned, and public insurance coverage of transition surgery was restored in 2017.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor may access private adult care under local protections, but a travelling minor cannot rely on local gender-affirming care and national rules may add funding or insurance obstacles.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names “radically pro-transgender” groups among priorities, and executive orders direct investigation of schools and teachers facilitating social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: This state/province has gender-identity hate-crime enhancements, abolished the panic defence, and a 2026 court enforced the civil-rights statute against an attacker of a transgender woman.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat-framing chills advocacy and can escalate scrutiny, but local courts and civil-rights enforcement provide a working remedy for ordinary street and service violations.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces the same national border/document scrutiny, state/province bans on gender-affirming care for minors, and a school sports ban whose status is unresolved.
minors_guardians.protection: State/province anti-bullying law covers gender identity, a 2024 court protected transgender students’ privacy and autonomy, and the care ban has a grandfather clause for existing treatment.
minors_guardians.interaction: The guardian cannot obtain local gender-affirming care for a trans minor visitor, and document mismatch at the border can expose both guardian and child to national refusal or inquiry.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A 2025 incident census recorded 72 anti-LGBTQ incidents here, second-highest raw count, though no per-capita denominator is published; one source calls this state/province the least safe in the region for trans residents after 2025 care restrictions.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate-crime enhancements have operated since 2019, the panic defence is abolished, the civil-rights statute is enforced in court, and 88% of residents polled supported discrimination protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police and courts are documented as responding to anti-trans violence, but the raw incident count and attributed “least safe” label keep street-level risk above the lowest tier.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National passport, entry, facilities and custody rules remain contested or variably enjoined; the traveller’s exposure depends on which measures are operating at the moment of travel.
remedies_unknowns.protection: A legal-aid FAQ tracks passport and identity-document rules, courts have enjoined several national orders, and local civil-rights remedies are documented as working.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies cannot reliably reach national border or custody decisions, and unresolved national litigation leaves the operative entry and facility rules uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Kestrelia denies entry after invasive questioning but expressly bars detention for marker discrepancy and retains only copies. Here national border rules can also trigger refusal, but add possible lifetime fraud inadmissibility and documented abusive national custody if detention follows, making this jurisdiction less safe than 0.35-C despite stronger local civil-rights protections.

Oakhaven’s rail inspectorate delays travel but ultimately issues a temporary permit after a supervisor applies transit guidelines. Here local anti-discrimination is strong, but the national border/facility/custody regime is not documented as yielding to local protection, so the combined encounter is materially less protected than 0.55-B.

Kestrel’s clinic director invokes a patient-privacy directive and resolves the refill under the visitor’s current name. This state/province has comparable local anti-discrimination and health-care protections, but national entry, facilities and custody exposures remain operative and are not cancelled by the local directive, placing the combined regime well below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The local state/province is one of the more protective layers in the dossier: public-accommodations and health-care anti-discrimination, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence repeal, and a 2026 civil-rights judgment give an outed trans visitor real local recourse and lower everyday service risk. But the national layer controls the journey’s highest-consequence points: passport/visa sex-marker screening, possible fraud-based permanent inadmissibility, government-funded single-sex facilities, immigration custody, and minor-care restrictions. Those national exposures are universal where they apply and are not documented as displaced by local law. The combined operative regime is therefore Elevated Risk: better than a hostile national regime with no local protection, but materially below Reduced Risk because border and custody consequences can be severe and local remedies do not reach them.
